originals.reason: Criterion branch is color-readback-review, never a negative: the initial query answered nothing and the disposable set/query/reset control in extensions.ts oscColorQueryProbe proves the readback path works for a value the embedder sets. Source audit: alacritty_terminal 0.26.0 src/term/color.rs:24-28 defines Colors::default() as [None; COUNT]; src/term/mod.rs:438 seeds Term::new with that empty array; src/term/mod.rs:1657-1671 stores an OSC-set colour as Some; src/term/mod.rs:1675-1688 answers a colour query through dynamic_color_sequence -> Event::ColorRequest(index, formatter), which carries an index and no value; vte 0.15.0 src/ansi.rs:1363-1387 (OSC 4) and :1421-1450 (OSC 10/11/12) split set from query and expose no default-colour reader. Termless packages/alacritty/native/src/lib.rs:312 builds Config::default() and no colour field exists anywhere in that Config (src/term/mod.rs:334-365), and :339-348 replies only when term.colors()[index] is Some. The default is therefore owned by the embedding application (alacritty's own event loop answers ColorRequest from its user config); a headless embed has no engine default to report and our adapter drops no value the engine holds. OSC 10;? is answered by nothing before an embedder sets it, while OSC 10;rgb:... -> set_color(index, color) makes the same query answer. Missing observable: an embedder-supplied default foreground colour.

originals.reason: Criterion branch is color-readback-review for the reset criteria: the initial colour query answered nothing, so the reset effect has no readback to compare. Source audit: OSC 110/111/112 call reset_color(NamedColor::Foreground/Background/Cursor) at vte 0.15.0 src/ansi.rs:1514-1521, and alacritty_terminal 0.26.0 src/term/mod.rs:1690-1701 implements reset as self.colors[index] = None; src/term/color.rs:24-28 makes that None the initial state of every slot at Term::new (src/term/mod.rs:438). The reset target is therefore the embedder's default colour, which the engine never holds: Termless packages/alacritty/native/src/lib.rs:339-348 replies only for Some(term.colors()[index]). OSC 110 restores None, so the post-reset query is silent by design and only an embedder-supplied default could answer it. Missing observable: an embedder-supplied default foreground colour.

originals.reason: Independent source review (@cto, 2026-10-31) of ghostty 0.4.0 WASM (ghostty-web ghostty-vt.wasm sha256 1f23e13db5bda55ab54943461b83a5d642bf8d2050a452fbe7871927383dfe9f, core ghostty 5714ed07a1012573261b7b7e3ed2add9c1504496, Termless d9d450554432336ace708b4efe1efa161dc1a087 tree 79960e87472dd0f65faef8a463aecc5041a70047): src/terminal/osc.zig (sha256 650bb29e387961edc78c6326e7c49be86ee88580d424b14b3acc0422a26d71b2) parses the OSC number one digit at a time: the .empty state at :556-566 admits leading digits 0, 1, 2, 4, 5, 7, 8 and 9 only and sets .invalid for anything else (so 3008 and 666 are invalid at the first digit); .@"17" at :779-793 accepts only ';' (176 invalid at its third digit); .@"4" at :902-919 accepts only ';' (440 invalid); .@"5" at :921-939 accepts ';' or '2' (555 invalid); .@"7" at :979-989 accepts ';' or '7' (710 invalid); an .invalid state yields no command, so the parser produces nothing for the terminal to act on. Measured in the cited run: fed "\u001b[1;1H\u001b[2K\u001b]3008;type=test\u0007X"; the sentinel X rendered at (0,0) and the engine exposed no OSC 3008 state (No systemd context target state is exposed at this pin). The engine does not implement OSC 3008 (context): unsupported. Re-bound 2026-10-31 to the first collection on the re-keyed WASM (run 56061219b20c0b01c3bbd18f3139a040, suite 61d992c009ff, terminfo edc0d4d8bf63d1fe7915df2dd4c3edec888d1388, termless d9d450554432336ace708b4efe1efa161dc1a087): the #32057 reply-path patch (termless d9d450554432336ace708b4efe1efa161dc1a087, vendor/ghostty-web only, zero OSC lines in its diff; adapter blobs index.ts f4b9d9f3 and backend.ts 603d090e unchanged) leaves the OSC parser unchanged, and the cell re-measured source-negative.

originals.reason: Independent source review (@cto, 2026-10-31) of ghostty 0.4.0 WASM (ghostty-web ghostty-vt.wasm sha256 1f23e13db5bda55ab54943461b83a5d642bf8d2050a452fbe7871927383dfe9f, core ghostty 5714ed07a1012573261b7b7e3ed2add9c1504496, Termless d9d450554432336ace708b4efe1efa161dc1a087 tree 79960e87472dd0f65faef8a463aecc5041a70047): src/terminal/osc.zig (sha256 650bb29e387961edc78c6326e7c49be86ee88580d424b14b3acc0422a26d71b2) parses the OSC number one digit at a time: the .empty state at :556-566 admits leading digits 0, 1, 2, 4, 5, 7, 8 and 9 only and sets .invalid for anything else (so 3008 and 666 are invalid at the first digit); .@"17" at :779-793 accepts only ';' (176 invalid at its third digit); .@"4" at :902-919 accepts only ';' (440 invalid); .@"5" at :921-939 accepts ';' or '2' (555 invalid); .@"7" at :979-989 accepts ';' or '7' (710 invalid); an .invalid state yields no command, so the parser produces nothing for the terminal to act on. Measured in the cited run: fed "\u001b[1;1H\u001b[2K\u001b]440;bell.wav\u0007X"; the sentinel X rendered at (0,0) and the engine exposed no OSC 440 state (No audio target state is exposed at this pin). The engine does not implement OSC 440 (audio): unsupported. Re-bound 2026-10-31 to the first collection on the re-keyed WASM (run 56061219b20c0b01c3bbd18f3139a040, suite 61d992c009ff, terminfo edc0d4d8bf63d1fe7915df2dd4c3edec888d1388, termless d9d450554432336ace708b4efe1efa161dc1a087): the #32057 reply-path patch (termless d9d450554432336ace708b4efe1efa161dc1a087, vendor/ghostty-web only, zero OSC lines in its diff; adapter blobs index.ts f4b9d9f3 and backend.ts 603d090e unchanged) leaves the OSC parser unchanged, and the cell re-measured source-negative.
